# One template set can hold sources parsed with different delimiters. A
# construction chain may call Delims more than once, and each ParseFS after it
# reads its files with whatever pair was last set.
#
# So the delimiters are not a property of the set. They are a property of each
# source, and every source has to be read with its own pair: reading either of
# these two files with the other's delimiters yields a tree with no actions.

muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- square.gohtml --
[[define "square"]]Hello, [[.Name]]![[end]]
-- curly.gohtml --
{{define "curly"}}Bye, {{.Name}}.{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(
	template.Must(
		template.New("t").Delims("[[", "]]").ParseFS(templateFiles, "square.gohtml"),
	).Delims("{{", "}}").ParseFS(templateFiles, "curly.gohtml"),
)

type Page struct {
	Name string
}

func Square(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "square", page)
}

func Curly(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "curly", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestSquare(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Square(&buf, Page{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Hello, World!"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("square = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestCurly(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Curly(&buf, Page{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Bye, World."; got != want {
		t.Errorf("curly = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
